newsitem.title: UK: UK"s Clarke says has no plans to levy VAT on food.
newsitem.headline: UK"s Clarke says has no plans to levy VAT on food.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday he had no plans to levy value added tax on food.
"I have no plans to impose VAT on food, I never have had any plans and the Labour Party know that perfectly well," he told parliament.
Last month, the opposition Labour Party accused the government of planning to levy VAT on food, which is currently zero-rated.
He said the Treasury's relationship with the Bank of England was working "perfectly well". The difference of opinion with Bank of England Governor Eddie George was small, he said.
On Wednesday, the Bank's quarterly inflation report urged a moderate increase in six percent base rates and forecast underlying inflation would be close to three percent and rising in two years time.
Clarke has refused to sanction a rate rise since a quarter-point increase on October 30.
